did: Week 46's Rust Rounds essay was refused for running 24 minutes against a 15 minute cap, and retried every hour for nothing. Rust Rounds essays may now run 30 minutes, while every other render keeps 15. A video the render policy refuses is no longer retried hourly: home holds it until something that decides it changes, such as the essay, the cap, the render or speaker image, the brand files or the worker itself, so week 46 renders on its first pass after deploy. The phone's renders board now says why a render was refused, too long or too large with the numbers, at contract epoch 15. Separately, four tab handlers now answer a busy database with 503 and a retry time instead of a 500. Before building the four-core Kokoro change, I found Kokoro is single-threaded on purpose, so that change is held for the owner.

calls.title: Only Rust Rounds essays get the 30 minute cap
options: Rust Rounds essays only; mock interview essays keep 15
Both essay kinds, since one recorder makes them
calls.why: The owner was asked about Rust Rounds essays only.
calls.undo: Add interview-essay to max_minutes in infra/render/render-calls.sh.

calls.title: A too-large refusal is held as well as a too-long one
options: Hold both too long and too large refusals
Hold only too long refusals made before recording
calls.why: The same input gives the same size, and every retry of a too-large video costs a full render.
calls.undo: Drop the REFUSED_LARGE branch of refusal in render-calls.sh and its tests.

calls.title: Kokoro's four-core change is held, not built
options: Hold it for the owner with the evidence
Build it anyway, since it is harmless
calls.why: Kokoro is single-threaded so its audio stays byte-identical, so four cores would not shorten a line; the coordinator agreed.
calls.undo: Raise kokoro's cpus and deploy limits to 4.0 in infra/compose/call-render.yml.

left: A retry floor or daily backstop for held refusals, because a clock needs the owner's call against home-compute's invariant 6 (server#940).
Kokoro to four cores, because Kokoro is single-threaded and the timeout fix is some-ui#3118 (server#941).
The tab reads still answer 422 on a busy database, a known AD4 tolerance filed as its own story (server#949).
The chrono and chrono-tz unmaintained advisories keep the allowed deny check red, which is the owner's call on ignoring or moving to jiff (server#953).
